methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units. Each unit represents a distinct requirement, feature, behavior, or constraint. The decomposition focused on identifying independent, self-contained, technically specific, and unambiguous elements that could be implemented as individual requirements. For the original research topic, this involved extracting explicit statements about sensor behavior, flow rate control, reset functionality, and water level conditions. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on identifying sensor inputs, output controls, Boolean expressions, truth table entries, and descriptions of combinational and sequential logic. The goal was to create sets of atomic units that could be compared to assess the coverage and similarity between the original topic and the generated specification.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The system controls water level in a reservoir.
Three active-high sensors (s[1], s[2], s[3]) are placed at 5-inch intervals.
Nominal flow valves (fr1, fr2, fr3) and a supplemental flow valve (dfr) control flow rate.
When water level is above s[3] (s[1], s[2], s[3] are high), all flow valves are closed (fr1, fr2, fr3, dfr are low).
When water level is between s[3] and s[2] (s[1], s[2] are high), only fr1 is asserted.
When water level is between s[2] and s[1] (s[1] is high), fr1 and fr2 are asserted.
When water level is below s[1] (no sensors are high), fr1, fr2, and fr3 are asserted.
If the water level increases, dfr is also asserted to increase the flow rate.
When the water level decreases, dfr is deasserted.
Active-high synchronous reset sets the system to a state where no sensors are asserted.
All flow rate outputs (fr1, fr2, fr3, dfr) are asserted after reset.
Reset simulates a prolonged low water level condition.
Module has flow rate control outputs fr3, fr2, fr1, and dfr
spec_atomic_units: Combinational logic determines flow rates (fr1, fr2, fr3) based on sensor inputs (s[3:1]).
Sensors: s[3], s[2], s[1]
Between s[3] and s[2]: s[1] & s[2] & ~s[3]
Between s[2] and s[1]: s[1] & ~s[2]
Below s[1]: ~s[1]
dfr requires sequential logic and is excluded from combinational logic.
s[3:1]: 3-bit input representing sensor states.
fr1: Controls the first nominal flow valve.
fr2: Controls the second nominal flow valve.
fr3: Controls the third nominal flow valve.
Truth table defines fr1, fr2, fr3 outputs for each sensor combination.
Simplified Boolean expressions for fr1, fr2, fr3 are provided.
Combinational logic can be implemented using standard logic gates.
Outputs change on the rising edge of clk.
Reset signal synchronously resets outputs.
Reset initializes the system to a state simulating a prolonged low water level.
Module has clock input clk
Module has reset input
Module has sensor inputs s[3:1]
Module has flow rate control outputs fr3, fr2, fr1, and dfr
